findings: The tool is not printed in the paper: l.1571 says only that the proof of prop:abs_max « applies as is », and B21 l.1093 asserts Sigma* is metrically complete without comparing the induced length of Sigma* with that of Sigma along their common part. Proved here: on points of Sigma* ∩ S (both in Reg M) the two chart systems are literally the same chart of Reg M, so densities, chart-Lipschitz, lengths and path lengths coincide.

On the rim r = R of a spear the S-length of the arc from angle phi1 to phi2 is exactly R|phi2 - phi1|, whatever tau_Sigma (the flat-chart velocity of phi -> D(tau(phi), R, phi + k) has Minkowski square R^2); so two rim points are at S-distance and at Sigma*-distance <= pi R. This is the estimate step (b) of the comment of LFSurgeryData.exists_isCompact_of_cauchySeq asks for.
questions: « The length of S » is read as DEC-31's LocalLengthSpace (e0SliceSys S) (BTZ points contribute 0), and « the length of Sigma* » as Causal.Flat.InducedLengthSpace 2 Sigma* in the flat charts of Reg M, as in RegCompleteLength; the comparison is stated for curves with the same points of M (pointwise, near a time, or on an open interval), which is what the tail argument uses.

kb_proposals: Causal.Flat.chartSys 2 T (T ⊆ Reg M) and GX.e0SliceSys S agree definitionally on common points (GX.chartSys_eq_e0SliceSys): compare Sigma*- and S-lengths by GX.pathLength_chartSys_eq_e0SliceSys / edist_inducedLength_le_pathLength_e0SliceSys (GXScaffold.BTZ.LengthCompare), never by re-deriving densities.

A spear's rim is SpearSurgeryDatum.rimPt φ = ψ(τ_Σ(R e^{iφ}), R e^{iφ}); the arc rimArc φ₁ φ₂ has S-length exactly R|φ₂ − φ₁| (pathLength_rimArc), any two rim points are joined in S ∩ cusp by a path of length ≤ π R (exists_rimPath), and LFSurgeryData.edist_rimPt_le gives the Σ*-distance bound.

The flat chart of Reg M along the rim is g • nullToMink (btzPaperNull (τ(φ), R, φ + k)) near φ₀ (SpearSurgeryDatum.eventually_regChart_rim, from eventually_regChart and arg(e^{i(φ−φ₀)}) = φ − φ₀ via Complex.arg_exp + toIocMod_eq_self).
